Google announced the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint that lets developers submit up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple‑choice, or rubric‑scoring questions in a single request.

The service returns calibrated confidence scores for each item and supports text, images, audio, video, and PDF inputs, all processed in one forward pass of the Gemini Decision 1 model.

Developers can start immediately by generating an API key in Google AI Studio and using the provided Python, JavaScript, or REST examples. The batch approach reduces both latency and cost compared with issuing separate calls for each question.

“Fast, calibrated decisions let us treat a whole class of routing problems as a single API call.”  

This matters because it enables real‑time query routing, content grading, and policy enforcement without building custom multimodal pipelines, offering a production‑grade building block that scales efficiently.

The API’s batch size and multimodal support are impressive, but it remains a closed‑set decision model, so it’s best suited for tasks with predefined answer sets.

How could batch‑processed confidence scores change the way your team handles content moderation or automated grading?
